outcome.reasoning:
Nitpicks: The agent wrapped the long title in quotation marks; the task didn’t forbid quotes and the underlying text appears to match exactly, so this is cosmetic.

Critical issues: The agent’s reported counts for (a) the number of top-level Parts and (b) the number of top-level Schedules are not supported by the provided DOM evidence. The DOM models confirm the agent did reach the as-enacted Introductory Text page (URL includes /introduction/enacted and the status explicitly says it is the original version). DOM state 3 explicitly shows the chapter line “2018 CHAPTER 12”, the full long title text, and the Royal Assent date “[23rd May 2018]”, so those three required Introductory Text deliverables are correctly captured in the correct version.

However, the task also requires counting top-level Parts and Schedules from the as-enacted table of contents. The available as-enacted contents DOM (state 1) only shows PART 1 and the beginning of PART 2, and none of the DOM states show the Schedules section at all. With no DOM evidence that the agent actually viewed the full TOC through all Parts and the Schedules list, the reported “7 Parts” and “20 Schedules” are effectively unverified assertions; from an outcome perspective, the user cannot rely on these counts as accurately recorded from the as-enacted table of contents.

Because those counts are a required part of the stopping condition and a key deliverable, the agent did not fully complete the task as intended even though it correctly captured the Introductory Text metadata.

A reasonable user would be flexible on minor formatting like adding quotation marks, but not flexible on incorrect counts or using the wrong (revised) version.
